title: Microbiome Assay with 96WP Updated April 2020
author: Priota Islam
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bfrqjm5w

steps.title: Prepare C. elegans L4s
steps.instruction: Pick 10 L4s onto each of 10 90mm OP50 seeded plates (total 100 L4s), for example, on Monday.

steps.title: Synchronize Worms by Bleaching
steps.instruction: Perform bleach synchronization of C. elegans at 2pm on the day of bleaching (e.g., Friday).

steps.title: Maintain Bleached N2s
steps.instruction: Keep the tube with bleached N2s on a rotator in a 20C incubator until refeed; do not exceed 5 days as worm behavior becomes inconsistent.

steps.title: Refeed Arrested L1s
steps.instruction: If tracking is planned for the following Thursday, refeed the arrested L1s onto four OP50 seeded 150mm plates on Monday (72 hours post-bleaching) at 2pm.

substeps.instruction: Store the refed L1 plates in a 20C incubator.

steps.title: Prepare No-Peptone NGM Agar
steps.instruction: At least 2 days prior to tracking day (e.g., Tuesday for a Thursday track), prepare approximately 250ml of no-peptone NGM.

steps.title: Dispense Agar into 96WP
steps.instruction: Dispense 200ul of agar into each well of the 96WP using the Integra ViaFill.

substeps.instruction: Measure the weight of the plates with lids on and record the average plate weight on the day of pouring.
Let the agar dry and store the plates at 4C (lid side down) for up to one week.

steps.title: Prepare Bacterial Cultures
steps.instruction: Two days prior to tracking (e.g., Tuesday afternoon for Thursday tracking), grow overnight cultures of the bacterial strain from the shuffled 96WP library stock plates.

substeps.instruction: Separately inoculate OP50 and incubate at 37C overnight in a shaking incubator at 200 rpm.
Remove bacterial cultures from incubators in the morning and store at 4C until seeding.

steps.title: Dry Agar-Filled Plates
steps.instruction: Remove agar-filled 96WPs from the cold room and dry in the drying cabinet for 2-3 hours.

substeps.instruction: Measure the weight of 3 plates without lids before drying.
Measure the weight of the 3 plates again after drying to ensure a weight loss of 3-5%.

steps.title: Seed Plates with Bacteria
steps.instruction: Seed the dried plates with the bacterial culture using the ViaFlo, dispensing 10ul volume into each well.

substeps.instruction: Edit protocol SAUL to include a mixing stage of 15 cycles to initially mix bacterial cultures and resuspend each strain.
Load long 12ul tips and adjust Z height based on test runs.
Mix the bacterial plate using the ViaFlo.
Edit protocol SAUL to change the mixing stage to 1 cycle for actual seeding.
Run the protocol to dispense 10ul per well.
Change tips every time a new plate is seeded.

steps.title: Post-Seeding Plate Storage
steps.instruction: Dry the seeded plates under the hood for 1 hour, then store them upside down in a closed box in the cold room (4C).

steps.title: Prepare and Dispense Worms
steps.instruction: On the day of tracking, prepare the worms and dispense them using the COPAS (wormsorter).

steps.title: Acclimatize Plates for Tracking
steps.instruction: Dry the plates for 30 minutes under the hood, then place them under the Hydra rig for another 30 minutes to acclimatize.

steps.title: Record Worm Tracking
steps.instruction: Record for 15 minutes using the script that involves blue light, with lids on and facing up inside the rig.

substeps.instruction: Wipe lids with lint-free tissues before placing under the rig.
Record each plate at four time points: 1hr, 3hrs, 5hrs, and 23.5hrs (next day).
Keep plates in the cave outside the rigs between the 1hr, 3hr, and 5hr time points.
Store plates in a 20C incubator overnight between the 5hr and 23.5hr time points.

steps.title: Cleanup
steps.instruction: Discard the plates in the biological waste bins after tracking is complete.
